root.name: Van't Kruijs Opening: Keoni-Hiva Gambit, Akahi Variation
root.moves: 1. e3 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3

overview: White plays an f4 gambit after 1.e3 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.f4 exf4 4.Nf3, a King's Gambit structure a tempo behind because e3 blocks the bishop. Black can keep the f4-pawn with ...g5 or ...d5 and develop freely while White hopes for d4 and piece activity. I am not sure of the theory here, so the evidence is kept short.

white_ideas.idea: Regain f4 with d4 and Bxf4, or build pressure with Nd5 and d4
Develop quickly and open lines against the black king

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...g5, ...d6 or ...d5
Develop calmly and return the pawn only for safety

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after e5 and f4 exchanges, Black pawn on f4 against White e3/d2

character.notes: An early pawn sacrifice with open lines and a weakened white king.

gambit.notes: White has played f4 and is a pawn down after ...exf4; Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: White's e3 move wastes a tempo compared with the King's Gambit, so the gambit is probably unsound.

structure.notes: Black e-pawn has gone and f-pawn is on f4, leaving open central lines.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Dubious gambit; a poor first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Ekolu and Alua Variations
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e3 e5 2. Nc3 d5 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3

character.reason: Early f4 gambit gives open lines and a loose white king.

gambit.reason: White offers the f-pawn after ...exf4 and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: A King's Gambit with an extra wasted tempo is hard to justify.

structure.reason: The e-pawn is traded and lines open towards both kings.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly choose 1.e3 and a gambit of this kind.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White's compensation is faster development for the pawn.
